actions.name: flow_tip_left
actions.why: Left tip-vortex corridor is only 0.18% covered and its declared span (0.04981 m) is the tightest of the three; level 3 gives 0.03125 m, a factor 1.6 below the requirement, and overlaps the wake box so the union is one equal-level block along the vortex path (no transition defect inside the corridor).

actions.name: flow_tip_right
actions.why: Mirror tip-vortex corridor with identical 0.04981 m span requirement; level 3 = 0.03125 m meets it. Spanwise symmetry is preserved exactly (Y bounds mirrored about 0) so the two rolled-up vortices are resolved with equal nominal cell size, which matters because at AR~2 the two vortices interact.

attempts.hypothesis: The mesh is a first attempt with no native failure evidence; the one measured, deterministic defect is that the off-body requirements are effectively unrefined (configured coverage 0.00386 / 0.00182 / 0.00181). Cause: refinement is purely distance-driven around the body (bands 0.03125 m @ L4 and 0.09375 m @ L3) plus one level-6 near-trailing-edge feature box; nothing follows the flow downstream of X=0.996. The trailing-edge vorticity sheet and the two tip-vortex corridors are transport features, not proximity features, so they must be prescribed explicitly. Fixing this with three flow_refine boxes at level 3 (0.25/2^3 = 0.03125 m) satisfies both declared spans with margin (wake 0.03125 < 0.06226 m; tips 0.03125 < 0.04981 m), keeps the level jump to the level-4 surface mesh at exactly one level (n_cells_between_levels=3 inserts a buffer), and is consistent with the existing level-3 outer distance band so the union is a single level-3 block with no internal transition. Level 3 is the coarsest level that meets the strict max axis span; level 2 (0.0625 m) would exceed the tip span (0.0625 > 0.0498) and would only pass via the native p95 1.5x tolerance, and level 4 would cost ~680k extra cells and break the 2M gate. I deliberately do NOT touch layers, first height, n_grow or snap: there is no native extrusion/quality evidence yet, and the planning y+ estimate (h1 = 1.1087e-3 m, y+~50, stack 0.01829 m) is a surrogate, not a measurement.

The native mechanism log confirms this is a squeeze-collapse, not an angle suppression: "Extruding 10578 out of 12069 faces (87.646%)" with 0 removed faces, and directional_outward_hit_distance finite_fraction = 0.0 at both caps and over the whole body — the outward normal-ray cohort finds no finite fluid gap, i.e. no wall-adjacent clearance is resolved there.
